name: Mezquita del Cristo de la Luz

position.source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/114522030 (centroid of the outline; long axis at 57.4°, the south-west façade on Calle Cristo de la Luz is the main one)

rights.note: Mosque of Bab al-Mardum, finished in December 999 (foundation inscription: built for Ahmad ibn Hadidi under the direction of Musa ibn Ali and Sa'ada); Mudéjar apse added about 1187. Owned by the Archdiocese of Toledo, open as a monument.

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q1324080_mezquita_del_cristo_de_la_luz.py, tools/meshkit.py) with AI assistance. The mosque of 999 in brick and masonry: on the south-west façade the three doorways (horseshoe and lobed arches with their alfiz), the band of interlaced blind arches, the sebka lattice, the brick inscription and the corbelled cornice, with the iron railing in front; on the north-west façade the three horseshoe arches inside round ones and the polylobed arches with two-colour voussoirs; blind arches on the south-east side. The Mudéjar apse of about 1187 with its straight bay and two tiers of blind arcades on a masonry plinth. The roofs are rarely seen and are estimated: a low tiled hip with the central bay raised a little, a half cone over the apse. The patio along the north-west façade (with the well and a palm) and the garden of Cristo de la Luz going down the slope in three terraces (levels from the IGN MDT05, ±1 m), with steps, a railing, the crossing paths and small pool of the chahar bagh and the trees from the orthophoto (positions ±2 m). The mirador over the Puerta del Sol and the inside (the nine vaults) are not modelled.
